messages:
ajohnson: Heads-up — customer reported weird billing after a resumed streaming request that fell back regions midway. They see tokens attributed to two different route tags and net billed > actual tokens.

sasha: Can you paste the minimal sequence? was this a user retry or router-initiated failover?

ajohnson: Looks like this: client opened stream -> router pinned to us-east -> model swapped to a lighter variant -> router rehomed to eu-west (fallback) -> client re-sent resume chunk. Server trimmed a conflicting prefix then accepted resume.

leo: That flow smells like double-counting: we charge the prefix at initial route then charge resumed suffix on fallback route without dedupe.

karla: From console POV customers see two separate ledger lines: one tagged `route:us-east-1` and one `route:eu-west-1`. No single "adjusted tokens" view. They file disputes immediately. UX wise we need a single line with breakdown and link to evidence.

sasha: Are there tool calls in the stream? those complicate attribution (we have to bill tool input vs model tokens).

ajohnson: Yes — stream included a side tool call mid-request. That tool call completed before the region move. So the stream had: prefix (A) -> toolcall -> suffix (B resumed). The ledger shows A charged on us-east, toolcall on us-east, B charged on eu-west.

leo: Two quick options: 1) attribute all tokens to origin route (first route) 2) attribute to where they actually executed (current). Both have pros/cons: (1) keeps charge locality predictable, (2) is more accurate to infra cost.

karla: Customers care about predictability. If we keep #2 we'll need console hints like "this request moved, charges split". Otherwise they'll get surprised.

sasha: Operationally, dedupe by session-id + token-offset would be ideal, but client resume offsets are sometimes flaky. We can rely on our resume ledger sequence numbers if we track per-session last-confirmed-offset.

ajohnson: Snippet from the router trace (sanitized):
```
ROUTER: session=abcd1234 pinned=us-east model=v1.2
MODEL_SWAP: session=abcd1234 model=v1.3 cost_delta=-0.6x
REHOME: session=abcd1234 -> eu-west (due to capacity)
RESUME: client chunk offset=128 server-trimmed-prefix=24 accepted
```

leo: That `server-trimmed-prefix` is the crux. We currently bill the trimmed tokens when they were generated but we don't mark them as "trimmed vs delivered" in the ledger. So when the client resumed we billed the resumed portion again.

karla: Could we add a console column `adjusted_tokens` and a hover explainer? Also an easy "dispute" button prepopulated with the session trace.

ajohnson: Two internal API proposals: add `billing_origin: initial_route|execution_route|session_consolidated` OR add a `session_billing_guid` that ties split charges together for UI aggregation. Thoughts?

sasha: I prefer `session_billing_guid` — less ambiguous and lets UI choose aggregation rules. But we should also emit `billing_reason` tags like `trimmed_prefix`, `retry_resume`, `fallback_rehome` so analytics can query.

leo: Agreed on GUID + reason tags. For ledger consumers (billing export) we can keep per-row route, but include `session_billing_guid` so customers can roll up. Billing export schema change needed.

karla: UX: show single collapsible entry labeled "Streaming session abcd1234 — net 3,420 tokens (split across 2 routes)" with a button "show raw ledger rows". Also show evidence: router trace + timestamps.

billing-bot: invoice_event: generated provisional charge lines for session abcd1234: 2100 tokens (us-east), 1600 tokens (eu-west) — total 3700 tokens.

ajohnson: Our net-delivered metrics show ~3420 tokens. So ~280 token discrepancy from trimmed prefix duplication.

leo: Action items I see: (A) short term: augment ledger rows with `session_billing_guid` and `billing_reason` to help console rollups + disputes; (B) medium: enforce dedupe when resume offset <= last_confirmed_offset; (C) long: make router prefer route-sticky during active streaming sessions to avoid mid-stream rehomes unless unavoidable.

karla: I'll design the rollup UI for (A). Quick mock in Figma and I'll share link.

sasha: For (B) we need: store last_confirmed_offset in session store, emit a dedupe decision in trace. We should also surface if client resume offset is untrusted.

ajohnson: I'll open an RFC for `session_billing_guid` + `billing_reason` fields on the internal meter API and add compat notes for billing export.

leo: I'll add a short-term reconciliation job to scan sessions with route splits and try to auto-merge obvious trimmed-prefix duplicates (non-authoritative, just flagging).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/eng-platform/session-ledger-guid-2026-03-22 will deploy to staging at 14:03 UTC :rocket:

karla: thx — ping me when staging has the ledger GUID visible so I can iterate UI tests.

ajohnson: Thanks all — feels like a plan. We'll prioritize the ledger tagging this sprint.

sasha: +1. Please add to eng-platform board and assign owners.

leo: Filed billing ticket BLG-892 with the scan plan and export schema change request.
